tenses_found: past perfect (had always had, had had enough, had done)
going to future in past (were going to fit)
grammatical_complexity.notes: Dominated by simple past tense. Past continuous and past perfect appear in a handful of sentences but are simple in form. Present perfect appears once. Overall the grammatical profile is basic with a few slightly more advanced structures appearing infrequently.

cultural_reference_load.notes: The cultural setting is entirely Latin American. Street names reference Latin American historical figures. Music references (cumbia, Celia Cruz, Marc Anthony) are well-known to the target learner. No North American-specific cultural knowledge needed.

sentence_structure.notes: Predominantly short, simple sentences with some compound sentences using 'and' and 'when'. A few sentences reach 12-14 words but most are under 12. Repetitive structure (they drove, they picked up, they put, they turned on sirens) aids comprehension.

items.context: The pair drove to the location and picked up the young girl.
items.reason: In this context, 'location' clearly means 'place' or 'position' — they drove to it. While Spanish 'locación' can refer to renting/leasing in real estate contexts, the driving context makes the meaning unambiguous. A Spanish speaker would not be confused here.
